speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a young patient presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand the severity of your condition, have you noticed if the skin lesions are itchy, painful, or spreading rapidly? Also, when did the fever and wrist pain first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of recent camping in Minnesota and a self-resolving knee infection raises concern for Lyme disease or disseminated gonococcal infection. Given your age and sexual activity, could you describe the appearance and location of your skin lesions, and do they change with movement? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential and CRP. REQUEST TEST: ESR. REQUEST IMAGES: Full_body_skin_examination.

text:
The Gram stain of your wrist fluid shows Gram-negative diplococci, which is highly specific for *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*. Combined with your recent travel, sexual activity, and migratory joint pain, this strongly suggests Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI).

DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
